qt: to the Commission Rosa Estaràs Ferragut (PPE) Subject:

The Cometa system, used for the remote monitoring of restraining orders in cases of genderbased violence in Spain, was plagued by signal losses, GPS geolocation failures and alarm delays, leaving women victims without protection. In September 2026, Spain’s Court of Auditors1 identified ‘serious deficiencies’. In response to a request for access to public information, the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) has confirmed that there is no notification in its records from the Ministry of Equality, which is responsible for the processing of these women’s data2. Article 33 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)3 requires the notification, within a maximum of 72 hours, of personal data breaches that pose a risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of this failure to notify the AEPD and has it requested information from the Spanish authorities?
Is that omission compatible with Article 33 of the GDPR, given the sensitivity of the data concerning the location of victims and perpetrators?
What steps does it intend to take to ensure Spain’s compliance with the GDPR, including the possible opening of infringement proceedings?
